The Restaurant and Menu Lifecycle\n142\t\n143\tA restaurant joins the platform through a registration step taken by a `PlatformAdmin`. Registration captures the restaurant's display `name` (non-empty, at most 120 characters, unique among active restaurants), its street `address`, and its geographic coordinates `lat` and `lng` in decimal degrees. A registered restaurant starts in `PENDING_APPROVAL`. The `PlatformAdmin` may specify a `commission_rate_override` at registration — a flat decimal rate in `[0.05, 0.35]` that, when set, supplants the tiered commission formula for that restaurant's orders — or leave it unset (the default is a null-meaning-tiered sentinel). `pending_settlement_cents` begins at 0.\n144\t\n145\tA separate approval step transitions the restaurant from `PENDING_APPROVAL` to `ACTIVE`. Only an `ACTIVE` restaurant is visible to customers and eligible to receive orders. A `PlatformAdmin` can later suspend an `ACTIVE` restaurant — moving it to `SUSPENDED` — or reinstate a `SUSPENDED` restaurant back to `ACTIVE`. Suspending an active restaurant additionally fans out a cancellation to every one of its orders that is currently in `PLACED`, transitioning each such order to `CANCELLED`; this fan-out is not counted against the transitive-cascade budget but is still atomic with the suspension itself. Each of these transitions is authored by a `PlatformAdmin`.\n146\t\n147\t`CLOSED` is a terminal lifecycle bucket for restaurants that have left the platform permanently; the full set of `Restaurant.status` values is `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, and `CLOSED`. Mutable restaurant fields — `address`, `lat`, `lng`, and `commission_rate_override` — can be edited by the owning `Restaurant` or by a `PlatformAdmin`; `name` is immutable after creation.\n148\t\n149\tA restaurant builds its catalog by creating `MenuItem` rows. Each menu item records the owning `restaurant_id`, the dish `name`, a `price_cents` value between 1 and 1 000 000, and an `is_listed` flag that defaults to true. The price and listing status of a menu item can be updated later by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`; unlisting an item removes it from customer view without destroying its historical identifier.\n150\t\n151\tAt the end of a settlement cycle, a `PlatformAdmin` triggers a payout by invoking the restaurant's settle capability. Settlement zeroes `pending_settlement_cents` (it does not negate or reverse the value — the accumulated balance is treated as paid out) and stands as the audit marker for that cycle. A settlement event is not itself modeled as a separate entity in the API surface.\n152\t\n153\t### 3.2. Customer Accounts\n154\t\n155\tA customer account is registered by a `PlatformAdmin` or by a `CustomerService` operator acting on the customer's behalf. The registration payload carries the customer's `name`, `phone` (unique across all customers), `address`, and geographic coordinates `lat` and `lng`. Two computed fields hang off the account: `credit_balance_cents`, a non-negative integer that accumulates platform credit from refunds and compensation and is drawn down before any fresh card charge on subsequent orders; and `trust_score`, a behavioral aggregate initialized at 1.0 and bounded to `[0.0, 1.0]`, which drops on abusive returns and climbs back on good-faith interactions.\n156\t\n157\tA customer can read only their own account; their `X-User-ID` must equal the `id` of the record they retrieve. `CustomerService` and `PlatformAdmin` may read any customer record in support of case work.\n158\t\n159\t### 3.3. Rider Lifecycle and Bonus Standing\n160\t\n161\tA rider joins the platform through a `PlatformAdmin` registration that captures `name` and `phone` (unique across all riders). New riders start in `OFFLINE`. The full set of `Rider.status` values is `OFFLINE`, `AVAILABLE`, `ON_DELIVERY`, and `SUSPENDED`.\n162\t\n163\tTo begin receiving dispatch offers, a rider invokes their go-online capability, transitioning from `OFFLINE` to `AVAILABLE`. Conversely, a rider may go offline only when no `Assignment` referring to them is currently in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`; attempting to go offline while any such assignment exists fails the state-machine precondition with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. Accepting an offer while `AVAILABLE` causes the system to set the rider to `ON_DELIVERY` automatically as a cascade. When the rider delivers an assignment and no other active assignments remain for them, the system returns them to `AVAILABLE`; when other active assignments remain (for example, the remaining legs of a merged route), the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`.\n164\t\n165\tA `PlatformAdmin` may suspend an `AVAILABLE` rider, but only when at least one of two performance thresholds is breached: the rider's `on_time_rate` must be strictly below 0.70, or the rider's `acceptance_rate` must be strictly below 0.50. Attempting to suspend a rider whose metrics are both at or above these thresholds is rejected with `ERR_SUSPEND_CRITERIA_NOT_MET`. `SUSPENDED` is terminal.\n166\t\n167\tFour rider metrics reflect recent performance. `on_time_rate` is the fraction of the rider's last 30 completed (`DELIVERED`) assignments that arrived by their promised time; it is initialized to 1.0 for riders with fewer than 10 completed deliveries, and constrained to `[0.0, 1.0]`. `acceptance_rate` is the fraction of the rider's last 30 dispatch offers (the union of `ACCEPTED` and `REJECTED` outcomes) that were accepted, likewise initialized to 1.0 and constrained to `[0.0, 1.0]`. `rating` is the arithmetic mean of customer ratings on the rider's last 30 completed deliveries on a 0-to-5 scale, initialized at 5.0. `wallet_balance_cents` is the rider's ledger — positive when they have unsettled earnings, negative when fines have outpaced earnings.\n168\t\n169\tFrom these three metrics the system derives each rider's `bonus_tier`. On every completed delivery (`PICKED_UP → DELIVERED` on an `Assignment`) and on every fine creation whose subject is that rider, the system recomputes the tier as follows. First, combine the three inputs with weights of 0.6 for `on_time_rate`, 0.3 for `acceptance_rate`, and 0.1 for the rider's rating normalized to the 0-to-1 interval by dividing `rating` by five. The weighted sum is rounded half-up to three decimal places. The resulting score is then mapped to a tier using inclusive lower-bound comparisons: a score of 0.90 or more is `PLATINUM`, a score of 0.80 or more but below 0.90 is `GOLD`, a score of 0.70 or more but below 0.80 is `SILVER`, and anything below 0.70 is `BRONZE`. A score of exactly 0.900 therefore lands in `PLATINUM`, not `GOLD`; a score of exactly 0.800 lands in `GOLD`, not `SILVER`; a score of exactly 0.700 lands in `SILVER`, not `BRONZE`. The four possible values of `bonus_tier` are `BRONZE`, `SILVER`, `GOLD`, and `PLATINUM`, with `BRONZE` as the default for a new rider. The only inputs to this recomputation are the three performance aggregates; fines in isolation do not feed the formula, though a late delivery that triggered a fine will have already moved `on_time_rate` downward for the same window and the score recomputation runs as part of the same cascade.\n170\t\n171\t### 3.4. Placing an Order\n172\t\n173\tAn order begins with a `Customer` issuing a placement request carrying three fields: the customer's own `customer_id`, the target `restaurant_id`, and an `items` array. Each entry in `items` specifies a `menu_item_id`, a snapshot `name` taken from the menu item at placement, a `unit_price_cents` pinned from the same snapshot, and a `quantity` of 1 or more. `items` must be non-empty. The order fails placement with `ERR_ORDER_INVALID` when `items` is empty, any quantity is below 1, or the resulting subtotal would be below 100 cents (the minimum order size). The target `Restaurant` must be `ACTIVE` and every `MenuItem` referenced must carry `is_listed` true and match the `Order.restaurant_id` — otherwise placement is rejected with `ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE`.\n174\t\n175\tWhen placement succeeds, the server computes six derived fields atomically. `subtotal_cents` is the sum across `items` of `unit_price_cents` multiplied by `quantity`. `distance_km` is the haversine great-circle distance from the restaurant's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`) to the customer's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`), expressed in kilometres and rounded to one decimal place. `is_peak` is set to true when the placement moment falls inside one of the two peak windows defined in §2.10 and frozen on the order at that moment. `promised_delivery_time` is set to the placement time plus 45 minutes.\n176\t\n177\t`provisional_delivery_fee_cents` is the solo-rider estimate of what the customer will pay for delivery. It is computed as a base of 300 cents, plus a per-kilometer surcharge of 120 cents for each whole kilometer band — where the band count is obtained by taking the ceiling of `distance_km` (so a 2.0-km distance produces 2 bands, while a 2.01-km distance produces 3 bands) and multiplying by 120, plus a peak surcharge of 200 cents whenever `is_peak` is true and zero cents otherwise. The provisional estimate does not model route merging, because merging is a runtime decision made only once a rider's current route is known.\n178\t\n179\t`provisional_commission_cents` is the tiered platform commission, priced at placement time. The tier structure is marginal: the first 20 000 cents of `subtotal_cents` is billed at 15%, the portion of the subtotal strictly between 20 000 and 50 000 cents is billed at 18%, and any portion above 50 000 cents is billed at 22%. The computation proceeds in a fixed evaluation order — first the tier-1 amount is determined as the minimum of `subtotal_cents` and 20 000, then the tier-2 amount as the excess over 20 000 up to 50 000, then the tier-3 amount as any further excess. Each tier's amount is multiplied by its rate, the three products are summed in decimal, and only the final sum is rounded half-up to a whole cent. Rounding each tier independently and then summing is forbidden because it produces a different answer on boundary subtotals.\n180\t\n181\tOrder placement also authorizes payment. `payment_status` starts at `UNPAID` and immediately moves to `AUTHORIZED` as a placement-time side effect; any available `credit_balance_cents` on the customer is drawn down before the card authorization covers the remaining amount. `final_delivery_fee_cents`, `final_commission_cents`, `actual_delivery_time`, and `minutes_late` all start as null and are populated only when the order reaches `DELIVERED`. `version` starts at 1, as for every other versioned resource.\n182\t\n183\t### 3.5. Restaurant-Side Order Flow\n184\t\n185\tA restaurant that owns the target order can accept it, transitioning the order from `PLACED` to `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`. Acceptance is only legal while the restaurant's own `status` is `ACTIVE` and the order is still in `PLACED`; the restaurant identity is enforced by the `X-User-ID` match against `Order.restaurant_id`. Acceptance does not touch `payment_status` — the order is already `AUTHORIZED` from placement. From `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, the restaurant signals start-preparing, advancing the order to `PREPARING`; this same action opens a dispatch offer to the best available rider, which may — depending on the current rider's route — merge into an existing `RouteGroup`. From `PREPARING`, the restaurant marks the order ready, advancing it to `READY_FOR_PICKUP`. Ready is only legal when a rider has already `ACCEPTED` the dispatch (or is further along at `PICKED_UP`) — the system refuses the ready transition otherwise with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.\n186\t\n187\tEither the customer or the restaurant (via rejection) may cancel an order while it is still in `PLACED`; the cancellation transitions the order to `CANCELLED` and moves `payment_status` from whichever of `UNPAID` or `AUTHORIZED` it is currently in to `VOIDED`. No charge has captured, so `credit_balance_cents` is not affected. `CustomerService` may also cancel on behalf of a customer. Cancellation once the order has moved beyond `PLACED` is not available through this channel; disputes at later stages flow through the refund workflow in §3.9.\n188\t\n189\tThe full set of `Order.status` values is `PLACED`, `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, and `REFUNDED`; the terminal states are `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REFUNDED`. The full set of `payment_status` values is `UNPAID`, `AUTHORIZED`, `CAPTURED`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`, `FULLY_REFUNDED`, and `VOIDED`.\n190\t\n191\t### 3.6. Dispatch, Assignment, and Route Merging\n192\t\n193\tWhen a restaurant starts preparing an order, the system opens a dispatch offer — an `Assignment` row linking an `order_id` to a candidate `rider_id`. An assignment begins in `OFFERED` at its `offered_at` timestamp and evolves through `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, and `DELIVERED` in the success path, or `REJECTED` / `CANCELLED` on abandonment. The full set of `Assignment.status` values is `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED`; `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED` are terminal.\n194\t\n195\tThe candidate `rider_id` is selected deterministically from the pool of riders whose `status` is `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY`. Any rider currently linked to an `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP` `Assignment` for the same `order_id` is excluded from this pool up front — the system never re-offers an order to a rider who already holds it, regardless of whether the offer originated from `/start-preparing`, from an explicit `/dispatch`, or from the fresh offer the system issues after a rejection or cancellation. From the surviving candidates the system prefers any rider in `ON_DELIVERY` whose existing `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` already contains at least one unpicked assignment whose pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of the new order's pickup restaurant — these are precisely the riders for whom acceptance would trigger the route-merge rule described two paragraphs below — over any rider in `AVAILABLE`. Within either preference tier the tie-breaker is `Rider.created_at` descending, so that the most recently registered rider wins; should that still tie, the rider whose `id` sorts lexicographically smallest is chosen. The presence of other live `Assignment` rows for the same `order_id` — including one already in `ACCEPTED` or `PICKED_UP` — is not by itself grounds for refusal; `/dispatch` always creates a new `OFFERED` `Assignment` so long as the pool is non-empty, and the uniqueness constraint stated in the next paragraph fires later at `/accept` time rather than at dispatch time. The dispatch is refused with `409 ERR_INVALID_STATE` only when the resulting candidate pool is empty, in which case no new `Assignment` is created.\n196\t\n197\tAcceptance by a rider requires that the rider's current `status` be `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY` (the latter is what enables route merging), that the corresponding `Order.status` be `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, or `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, and — critically — that no other `Assignment` already exists for the same `order_id` in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`. When two riders race to accept the same dispatched offer, first-writer-wins on this uniqueness constraint: exactly one assignment advances to `ACCEPTED`, and the losing attempt is rejected with `ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. Acceptance stamps `accepted_at`, cascades the rider's `status` to `ON_DELIVERY` if they were `AVAILABLE`, and triggers a recomputation of `acceptance_rate` over the rider's last 30 offers.\n198\t\n199\tRoute merging happens at the same moment. When the accepting rider already holds an `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` and the newly accepted order's pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of an existing unpicked assignment's pickup restaurant, the new assignment is attached to that `RouteGroup` — its `route_group_id` is set to the group's `id` and the group's `assignment_ids` array is extended to include the new assignment's `id`. The `RouteGroup` itself tracks its own `rider_id`, `assignment_ids`, `merged_at` timestamp, and `status`, which spans `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, and `ABANDONED`, starting in `ACTIVE`. Solo deliveries leave `route_group_id` null.\n200\t\n201\tRejection of an offer — either explicitly by the rider, or via the 60-second offer-timeout sweep that runs as part of the clock-advance capability — moves the assignment to `REJECTED`, recomputes the rider's `acceptance_rate`, and spawns a fresh `Assignment` for the order targeting the next best available rider.\n202\t\n203\tPickup advances the assignment from `ACCEPTED` to `PICKED_UP`, stamps `picked_up_at`, and cascades the order from `READY_FOR_PICKUP` to `PICKED_UP`. A rider may also cancel an assignment after accepting it but before pickup; this transition is legal only while the assignment is in `ACCEPTED` and the order has not yet reached `PICKED_UP`. Cancellation creates a `Fine` whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `RIDER_NO_SHOW`, with `amount_cents` fixed at 500 — the flat no-show penalty. That fine in turn debits the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by 500 cents and triggers a `bonus_tier` recomputation (this is the transitive chain: the assignment cancellation triggers the fine, and the fine's creation triggers the wallet debit and tier recompute). The system then dispatches a fresh offer for the same order to the next best rider.\n204\t\n205\t### 3.7. Delivery and Fiscal Reconciliation\n206\t\n207\tThe final operational step is delivery. A rider whose assignment is in `PICKED_UP` and whose corresponding order is in `PICKED_UP` invokes the deliver capability. The assignment transitions to `DELIVERED`, `delivered_at` is stamped, and the order cascades to `DELIVERED` as well. A substantial chain of fiscal side-effects fires atomically on this cascade.\n208\t\n209\tFirst, the order's `actual_delivery_time` is set to the current instant, and `minutes_late` is computed as the non-negative floor of the seconds between `actual_delivery_time` and `promised_delivery_time`, divided by 60. Early or on-time deliveries produce a `minutes_late` of zero.\n210\t\n211\tSecond, the order's `final_delivery_fee_cents` is reconciled from the frozen placement inputs. The solo-style fee is recomputed from the original `distance_km` and `is_peak` snapshots using the same base-of-300, 120-per-band, 200-peak formula as the provisional fee. Then, if the assignment carries a non-null `route_group_id` and its route group contains two or more assignments, a 25% route-merge discount is applied: the discount is computed as the floor of the solo fee times 0.25, and the rider-facing delivery fee is the solo fee minus that discount. Solo deliveries (no `route_group_id`, or a `RouteGroup` containing only this assignment) carry no discount and the final fee equals the solo fee. The reconciled amount is written to both `Order.final_delivery_fee_cents` and `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` — these two mirror each other for any single-leg delivery, and for merged deliveries the platform absorbs the discount as a cost of bundling.\n212\t\n213\tThird, the order's `final_commission_cents` is reconciled — and this is where it may diverge from `provisional_commission_cents`. If, at the moment of delivery, the owning restaurant's `commission_rate_override` is a non-null decimal, commission is computed as a flat rate: the subtotal multiplied by that override rate, rounded half-up to a whole cent. The override applies to the entire subtotal, not just the portion above any tier threshold. If `commission_rate_override` is null at delivery time, the same tiered formula described in §3.4 runs again — 15% / 18% / 22% across the same 20 000-cent and 50 000-cent caps, summed in decimal and then rounded half-up once. Because the override can be changed mid-flight by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`, the final commission can legitimately differ from the provisional one even though the subtotal is immutable.\n214\t\n215\tFourth, `payment_status` moves unconditionally to `CAPTURED`.\n216\t\n217\tFifth, if `minutes_late` is greater than zero, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `LATE_DELIVERY`. The fine amount is tiered: when `minutes_late` is from 1 through 10 inclusive, `amount_cents` is a flat 200 cents (a two-dollar penalty); when `minutes_late` is from 11 through 30 inclusive, `amount_cents` is 500 plus 50 per minute over 10 — so a 20-minute lateness yields 500 plus 50 times 10, which is 1 000 cents; when `minutes_late` exceeds 30, `amount_cents` is the smaller of `final_delivery_fee_cents` and 1 500 (the rider's earnings clawback is capped at $15 regardless of the fee) plus an additional 500 cents of customer compensation. This fine creation itself triggers a follow-on debit of the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by `amount_cents` and a recomputation of the rider's `bonus_tier` — the same transitive fan-out chain as the no-show case.\n218\t\n219\tSixth, the owning restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is incremented by `subtotal_cents` minus `final_commission_cents` — the restaurant's slice of the order.\n220\t\n221\tSeventh, the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited with the reconciled `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` (net of any merge discount absorbed by the platform) and the rider's `bonus_tier` is recomputed a final time for the delivery event.\n222\t\n223\tEighth, if the assignment belonged to a `RouteGroup` and every peer assignment in that group has also reached `DELIVERED`, the `RouteGroup` transitions from `ACTIVE` to `COMPLETED`. Otherwise the group stays `ACTIVE` and the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`. A rider only returns to `AVAILABLE` once no active assignments remain for them.\n224\t\n225\tAll of these effects happen as part of the same request. A single rider delivery therefore mutates the assignment, the order, the restaurant, the rider, the fine (when created), and potentially the route group — and each versioned resource in that chain has its `updated_at` refreshed and its `version` incremented exactly once.\n226\t\n227\t### 3.8. Restaurant Settlement\n228\t\n229\tAt each payout cycle, the platform settles with each `ACTIVE` restaurant. A `PlatformAdmin` invokes the restaurant's settle capability; the restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is reset to 0, and the settlement event is treated as the paid-out audit marker. Returns that were approved after a delivery but before the settlement cycle decrement `pending_settlement_cents` at the moment of approval (see §3.9); deliveries increment it. Because both updates are performed atomically as part of the triggering request, the running aggregate is always consistent with the set of `Order` rows in `DELIVERED` that have not been `FULLY_REFUNDED`. The aggregate is never recomputed from scratch; each event applies an incremental delta.\n230\t\n231\t### 3.9. Returns and Refunds\n232\t\n233\tA customer may open a return on a delivered order. The customer-facing payload carries the return's `reason` — one of `QUALITY_ISSUE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `LATE`, or `OTHER` — and a `requested_refund_cents` amount. The request is only eligible when the order is in `DELIVERED` and the current moment is within 24 hours of the order's `actual_delivery_time`; requests outside that window are rejected with `ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED`. The requested refund must be at least 1 and at most the order's `subtotal_cents`; values out of range are rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. A duplicate return attempt — a request made while another `Return` for the same order is already in `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, or `ESCALATED` — is rejected with `ERR_DUPLICATE_RETURN`.\n234\t\n235\tA successful return request creates a `Return` row in `REQUESTED` carrying the `order_id`, the `reason`, the `requested_refund_cents`, and — at decision time — the `reviewer_cs_user_id` that recorded the outcome. The owning `Order` transitions from `DELIVERED` to `REFUND_REQUESTED`. The full set of `Return.status` values is `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, and `ESCALATED`; `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` are terminal.\n236\t\n237\tA `CustomerService` operator then reviews. Approval carries an `approved_refund_cents` amount that must be at least 1, at most the order's `subtotal_cents`, and at most the originally requested refund — any violation is rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. On approval, the `Return` moves to `APPROVED` and the owning order cascades from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `REFUNDED`. The order's `payment_status` becomes `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` if `approved_refund_cents` is strictly less than `subtotal_cents`, or `FULLY_REFUNDED` if the approved amount equals the subtotal. The customer's `credit_balance_cents` is credited by `approved_refund_cents`. The restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is decremented by the same amount. And finally, if the customer's `trust_score` is strictly below 0.5 and the return's `reason` is `QUALITY_ISSUE`, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the customer and whose `reason` is `ABUSIVE_RETURN` with `amount_cents` equal to `approved_refund_cents`. The four possible `Fine.reason` values are `LATE_DELIVERY`, `ABUSIVE_RETURN`, `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT`, and `RIDER_NO_SHOW`; a fine's `subject_type` is one of `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER` and its `subject_id` is the matching entity's `id`. A fine's `settlement_status` begins at `PENDING` and can move to `SETTLED` (when the underlying wallet or settlement event has cleared the balance) or `WAIVED` (when a `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` forgives the debit and reverses any wallet or credit adjustment).\n238\t\n239\tRejection by a `CustomerService` operator moves the `Return` to `REJECTED` and reverts the order from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `DELIVERED` with no monetary change. Escalation moves the `Return` from `REQUESTED` to `ESCALATED` and opens a `WorkOrder` linked via `related_return_id` for supervisor attention. An escalated return can be brought back to `REQUESTED` through a reopen step — this closes the linked `WorkOrder`. The approve / reject transitions accept both `REQUESTED` and `ESCALATED` as legal starting states; the reopen transition is only legal from `ESCALATED`."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"26210b47-8c4c-40f2-a620-28f8a09c960f","uuid":"b4145563-4253-45e4-966f-25331aad4234","timestamp":"2026-05-21T10:39:46.136Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/app/PRD.md","content":"\n### 3.1. The Restaurant and Menu Lifecycle\n\nA restaurant joins the platform through a registration step taken by a `PlatformAdmin`. Registration captures the restaurant's display `name` (non-empty, at most 120 characters, unique among active restaurants), its street `address`, and its geographic coordinates `lat` and `lng` in decimal degrees. A registered restaurant starts in `PENDING_APPROVAL`. The `PlatformAdmin` may specify a `commission_rate_override` at registration — a flat decimal rate in `[0.05, 0.35]` that, when set, supplants the tiered commission formula for that restaurant's orders — or leave it unset (the default is a null-meaning-tiered sentinel). `pending_settlement_cents` begins at 0.\n\nA separate approval step transitions the restaurant from `PENDING_APPROVAL` to `ACTIVE`. Only an `ACTIVE` restaurant is visible to customers and eligible to receive orders. A `PlatformAdmin` can later suspend an `ACTIVE` restaurant — moving it to `SUSPENDED` — or reinstate a `SUSPENDED` restaurant back to `ACTIVE`. Suspending an active restaurant additionally fans out a cancellation to every one of its orders that is currently in `PLACED`, transitioning each such order to `CANCELLED`; this fan-out is not counted against the transitive-cascade budget but is still atomic with the suspension itself. Each of these transitions is authored by a `PlatformAdmin`.\n\n`CLOSED` is a terminal lifecycle bucket for restaurants that have left the platform permanently; the full set of `Restaurant.status` values is `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, and `CLOSED`. Mutable restaurant fields — `address`, `lat`, `lng`, and `commission_rate_override` — can be edited by the owning `Restaurant` or by a `PlatformAdmin`; `name` is immutable after creation.\n\nA restaurant builds its catalog by creating `MenuItem` rows. Each menu item records the owning `restaurant_id`, the dish `name`, a `price_cents` value between 1 and 1 000 000, and an `is_listed` flag that defaults to true. The price and listing status of a menu item can be updated later by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`; unlisting an item removes it from customer view without destroying its historical identifier.\n\nAt the end of a settlement cycle, a `PlatformAdmin` triggers a payout by invoking the restaurant's settle capability. Settlement zeroes `pending_settlement_cents` (it does not negate or reverse the value — the accumulated balance is treated as paid out) and stands as the audit marker for that cycle. A settlement event is not itself modeled as a separate entity in the API surface.\n\n### 3.2. Customer Accounts\n\nA customer account is registered by a `PlatformAdmin` or by a `CustomerService` operator acting on the customer's behalf. The registration payload carries the customer's `name`, `phone` (unique across all customers), `address`, and geographic coordinates `lat` and `lng`. Two computed fields hang off the account: `credit_balance_cents`, a non-negative integer that accumulates platform credit from refunds and compensation and is drawn down before any fresh card charge on subsequent orders; and `trust_score`, a behavioral aggregate initialized at 1.0 and bounded to `[0.0, 1.0]`, which drops on abusive returns and climbs back on good-faith interactions.\n\nA customer can read only their own account; their `X-User-ID` must equal the `id` of the record they retrieve. `CustomerService` and `PlatformAdmin` may read any customer record in support of case work.\n\n### 3.3. Rider Lifecycle and Bonus Standing\n\nA rider joins the platform through a `PlatformAdmin` registration that captures `name` and `phone` (unique across all riders). New riders start in `OFFLINE`. The full set of `Rider.status` values is `OFFLINE`, `AVAILABLE`, `ON_DELIVERY`, and `SUSPENDED`.\n\nTo begin receiving dispatch offers, a rider invokes their go-online capability, transitioning from `OFFLINE` to `AVAILABLE`. Conversely, a rider may go offline only when no `Assignment` referring to them is currently in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`; attempting to go offline while any such assignment exists fails the state-machine precondition with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. Accepting an offer while `AVAILABLE` causes the system to set the rider to `ON_DELIVERY` automatically as a cascade. When the rider delivers an assignment and no other active assignments remain for them, the system returns them to `AVAILABLE`; when other active assignments remain (for example, the remaining legs of a merged route), the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`.\n\nA `PlatformAdmin` may suspend an `AVAILABLE` rider, but only when at least one of two performance thresholds is breached: the rider's `on_time_rate` must be strictly below 0.70, or the rider's `acceptance_rate` must be strictly below 0.50. Attempting to suspend a rider whose metrics are both at or above these thresholds is rejected with `ERR_SUSPEND_CRITERIA_NOT_MET`. `SUSPENDED` is terminal.\n\nFour rider metrics reflect recent performance. `on_time_rate` is the fraction of the rider's last 30 completed (`DELIVERED`) assignments that arrived by their promised time; it is initialized to 1.0 for riders with fewer than 10 completed deliveries, and constrained to `[0.0, 1.0]`. `acceptance_rate` is the fraction of the rider's last 30 dispatch offers (the union of `ACCEPTED` and `REJECTED` outcomes) that were accepted, likewise initialized to 1.0 and constrained to `[0.0, 1.0]`. `rating` is the arithmetic mean of customer ratings on the rider's last 30 completed deliveries on a 0-to-5 scale, initialized at 5.0. `wallet_balance_cents` is the rider's ledger — positive when they have unsettled earnings, negative when fines have outpaced earnings.\n\nFrom these three metrics the system derives each rider's `bonus_tier`. On every completed delivery (`PICKED_UP → DELIVERED` on an `Assignment`) and on every fine creation whose subject is that rider, the system recomputes the tier as follows. First, combine the three inputs with weights of 0.6 for `on_time_rate`, 0.3 for `acceptance_rate`, and 0.1 for the rider's rating normalized to the 0-to-1 interval by dividing `rating` by five. The weighted sum is rounded half-up to three decimal places. The resulting score is then mapped to a tier using inclusive lower-bound comparisons: a score of 0.90 or more is `PLATINUM`, a score of 0.80 or more but below 0.90 is `GOLD`, a score of 0.70 or more but below 0.80 is `SILVER`, and anything below 0.70 is `BRONZE`. A score of exactly 0.900 therefore lands in `PLATINUM`, not `GOLD`; a score of exactly 0.800 lands in `GOLD`, not `SILVER`; a score of exactly 0.700 lands in `SILVER`, not `BRONZE`. The four possible values of `bonus_tier` are `BRONZE`, `SILVER`, `GOLD`, and `PLATINUM`, with `BRONZE` as the default for a new rider. The only inputs to this recomputation are the three performance aggregates; fines in isolation do not feed the formula, though a late delivery that triggered a fine will have already moved `on_time_rate` downward for the same window and the score recomputation runs as part of the same cascade.\n\n### 3.4. Placing an Order\n\nAn order begins with a `Customer` issuing a placement request carrying three fields: the customer's own `customer_id`, the target `restaurant_id`, and an `items` array. Each entry in `items` specifies a `menu_item_id`, a snapshot `name` taken from the menu item at placement, a `unit_price_cents` pinned from the same snapshot, and a `quantity` of 1 or more. `items` must be non-empty. The order fails placement with `ERR_ORDER_INVALID` when `items` is empty, any quantity is below 1, or the resulting subtotal would be below 100 cents (the minimum order size). The target `Restaurant` must be `ACTIVE` and every `MenuItem` referenced must carry `is_listed` true and match the `Order.restaurant_id` — otherwise placement is rejected with `ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE`.\n\nWhen placement succeeds, the server computes six derived fields atomically. `subtotal_cents` is the sum across `items` of `unit_price_cents` multiplied by `quantity`. `distance_km` is the haversine great-circle distance from the restaurant's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`) to the customer's coordinates (`lat`, `lng`), expressed in kilometres and rounded to one decimal place. `is_peak` is set to true when the placement moment falls inside one of the two peak windows defined in §2.10 and frozen on the order at that moment. `promised_delivery_time` is set to the placement time plus 45 minutes.\n\n`provisional_delivery_fee_cents` is the solo-rider estimate of what the customer will pay for delivery. It is computed as a base of 300 cents, plus a per-kilometer surcharge of 120 cents for each whole kilometer band — where the band count is obtained by taking the ceiling of `distance_km` (so a 2.0-km distance produces 2 bands, while a 2.01-km distance produces 3 bands) and multiplying by 120, plus a peak surcharge of 200 cents whenever `is_peak` is true and zero cents otherwise. The provisional estimate does not model route merging, because merging is a runtime decision made only once a rider's current route is known.\n\n`provisional_commission_cents` is the tiered platform commission, priced at placement time. The tier structure is marginal: the first 20 000 cents of `subtotal_cents` is billed at 15%, the portion of the subtotal strictly between 20 000 and 50 000 cents is billed at 18%, and any portion above 50 000 cents is billed at 22%. The computation proceeds in a fixed evaluation order — first the tier-1 amount is determined as the minimum of `subtotal_cents` and 20 000, then the tier-2 amount as the excess over 20 000 up to 50 000, then the tier-3 amount as any further excess. Each tier's amount is multiplied by its rate, the three products are summed in decimal, and only the final sum is rounded half-up to a whole cent. Rounding each tier independently and then summing is forbidden because it produces a different answer on boundary subtotals.\n\nOrder placement also authorizes payment. `payment_status` starts at `UNPAID` and immediately moves to `AUTHORIZED` as a placement-time side effect; any available `credit_balance_cents` on the customer is drawn down before the card authorization covers the remaining amount. `final_delivery_fee_cents`, `final_commission_cents`, `actual_delivery_time`, and `minutes_late` all start as null and are populated only when the order reaches `DELIVERED`. `version` starts at 1, as for every other versioned resource.\n\n### 3.5. Restaurant-Side Order Flow\n\nA restaurant that owns the target order can accept it, transitioning the order from `PLACED` to `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`. Acceptance is only legal while the restaurant's own `status` is `ACTIVE` and the order is still in `PLACED`; the restaurant identity is enforced by the `X-User-ID` match against `Order.restaurant_id`. Acceptance does not touch `payment_status` — the order is already `AUTHORIZED` from placement. From `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, the restaurant signals start-preparing, advancing the order to `PREPARING`; this same action opens a dispatch offer to the best available rider, which may — depending on the current rider's route — merge into an existing `RouteGroup`. From `PREPARING`, the restaurant marks the order ready, advancing it to `READY_FOR_PICKUP`. Ready is only legal when a rider has already `ACCEPTED` the dispatch (or is further along at `PICKED_UP`) — the system refuses the ready transition otherwise with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.\n\nEither the customer or the restaurant (via rejection) may cancel an order while it is still in `PLACED`; the cancellation transitions the order to `CANCELLED` and moves `payment_status` from whichever of `UNPAID` or `AUTHORIZED` it is currently in to `VOIDED`. No charge has captured, so `credit_balance_cents` is not affected. `CustomerService` may also cancel on behalf of a customer. Cancellation once the order has moved beyond `PLACED` is not available through this channel; disputes at later stages flow through the refund workflow in §3.9.\n\nThe full set of `Order.status` values is `PLACED`, `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, and `REFUNDED`; the terminal states are `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REFUNDED`. The full set of `payment_status` values is `UNPAID`, `AUTHORIZED`, `CAPTURED`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`, `FULLY_REFUNDED`, and `VOIDED`.\n\n### 3.6. Dispatch, Assignment, and Route Merging\n\nWhen a restaurant starts preparing an order, the system opens a dispatch offer — an `Assignment` row linking an `order_id` to a candidate `rider_id`. An assignment begins in `OFFERED` at its `offered_at` timestamp and evolves through `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, and `DELIVERED` in the success path, or `REJECTED` / `CANCELLED` on abandonment. The full set of `Assignment.status` values is `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED`; `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED` are terminal.\n\nThe candidate `rider_id` is selected deterministically from the pool of riders whose `status` is `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY`. Any rider currently linked to an `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP` `Assignment` for the same `order_id` is excluded from this pool up front — the system never re-offers an order to a rider who already holds it, regardless of whether the offer originated from `/start-preparing`, from an explicit `/dispatch`, or from the fresh offer the system issues after a rejection or cancellation. From the surviving candidates the system prefers any rider in `ON_DELIVERY` whose existing `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` already contains at least one unpicked assignment whose pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of the new order's pickup restaurant — these are precisely the riders for whom acceptance would trigger the route-merge rule described two paragraphs below — over any rider in `AVAILABLE`. Within either preference tier the tie-breaker is `Rider.created_at` descending, so that the most recently registered rider wins; should that still tie, the rider whose `id` sorts lexicographically smallest is chosen. The presence of other live `Assignment` rows for the same `order_id` — including one already in `ACCEPTED` or `PICKED_UP` — is not by itself grounds for refusal; `/dispatch` always creates a new `OFFERED` `Assignment` so long as the pool is non-empty, and the uniqueness constraint stated in the next paragraph fires later at `/accept` time rather than at dispatch time. The dispatch is refused with `409 ERR_INVALID_STATE` only when the resulting candidate pool is empty, in which case no new `Assignment` is created.\n\nAcceptance by a rider requires that the rider's current `status` be `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY` (the latter is what enables route merging), that the corresponding `Order.status` be `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, or `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, and — critically — that no other `Assignment` already exists for the same `order_id` in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`. When two riders race to accept the same dispatched offer, first-writer-wins on this uniqueness constraint: exactly one assignment advances to `ACCEPTED`, and the losing attempt is rejected with `ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. Acceptance stamps `accepted_at`, cascades the rider's `status` to `ON_DELIVERY` if they were `AVAILABLE`, and triggers a recomputation of `acceptance_rate` over the rider's last 30 offers.\n\nRoute merging happens at the same moment. When the accepting rider already holds an `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` and the newly accepted order's pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of an existing unpicked assignment's pickup restaurant, the new assignment is attached to that `RouteGroup` — its `route_group_id` is set to the group's `id` and the group's `assignment_ids` array is extended to include the new assignment's `id`. The `RouteGroup` itself tracks its own `rider_id`, `assignment_ids`, `merged_at` timestamp, and `status`, which spans `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, and `ABANDONED`, starting in `ACTIVE`. Solo deliveries leave `route_group_id` null.\n\nRejection of an offer — either explicitly by the rider, or via the 60-second offer-timeout sweep that runs as part of the clock-advance capability — moves the assignment to `REJECTED`, recomputes the rider's `acceptance_rate`, and spawns a fresh `Assignment` for the order targeting the next best available rider.\n\nPickup advances the assignment from `ACCEPTED` to `PICKED_UP`, stamps `picked_up_at`, and cascades the order from `READY_FOR_PICKUP` to `PICKED_UP`. A rider may also cancel an assignment after accepting it but before pickup; this transition is legal only while the assignment is in `ACCEPTED` and the order has not yet reached `PICKED_UP`. Cancellation creates a `Fine` whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `RIDER_NO_SHOW`, with `amount_cents` fixed at 500 — the flat no-show penalty. That fine in turn debits the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by 500 cents and triggers a `bonus_tier` recomputation (this is the transitive chain: the assignment cancellation triggers the fine, and the fine's creation triggers the wallet debit and tier recompute). The system then dispatches a fresh offer for the same order to the next best rider.\n\n### 3.7. Delivery and Fiscal Reconciliation\n\nThe final operational step is delivery. A rider whose assignment is in `PICKED_UP` and whose corresponding order is in `PICKED_UP` invokes the deliver capability. The assignment transitions to `DELIVERED`, `delivered_at` is stamped, and the order cascades to `DELIVERED` as well. A substantial chain of fiscal side-effects fires atomically on this cascade.\n\nFirst, the order's `actual_delivery_time` is set to the current instant, and `minutes_late` is computed as the non-negative floor of the seconds between `actual_delivery_time` and `promised_delivery_time`, divided by 60. Early or on-time deliveries produce a `minutes_late` of zero.\n\nSecond, the order's `final_delivery_fee_cents` is reconciled from the frozen placement inputs. The solo-style fee is recomputed from the original `distance_km` and `is_peak` snapshots using the same base-of-300, 120-per-band, 200-peak formula as the provisional fee. Then, if the assignment carries a non-null `route_group_id` and its route group contains two or more assignments, a 25% route-merge discount is applied: the discount is computed as the floor of the solo fee times 0.25, and the rider-facing delivery fee is the solo fee minus that discount. Solo deliveries (no `route_group_id`, or a `RouteGroup` containing only this assignment) carry no discount and the final fee equals the solo fee. The reconciled amount is written to both `Order.final_delivery_fee_cents` and `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` — these two mirror each other for any single-leg delivery, and for merged deliveries the platform absorbs the discount as a cost of bundling.\n\nThird, the order's `final_commission_cents` is reconciled — and this is where it may diverge from `provisional_commission_cents`. If, at the moment of delivery, the owning restaurant's `commission_rate_override` is a non-null decimal, commission is computed as a flat rate: the subtotal multiplied by that override rate, rounded half-up to a whole cent. The override applies to the entire subtotal, not just the portion above any tier threshold. If `commission_rate_override` is null at delivery time, the same tiered formula described in §3.4 runs again — 15% / 18% / 22% across the same 20 000-cent and 50 000-cent caps, summed in decimal and then rounded half-up once. Because the override can be changed mid-flight by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`, the final commission can legitimately differ from the provisional one even though the subtotal is immutable.\n\nFourth, `payment_status` moves unconditionally to `CAPTURED`.\n\nFifth, if `minutes_late` is greater than zero, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `LATE_DELIVERY`. The fine amount is tiered: when `minutes_late` is from 1 through 10 inclusive, `amount_cents` is a flat 200 cents (a two-dollar penalty); when `minutes_late` is from 11 through 30 inclusive, `amount_cents` is 500 plus 50 per minute over 10 — so a 20-minute lateness yields 500 plus 50 times 10, which is 1 000 cents; when `minutes_late` exceeds 30, `amount_cents` is the smaller of `final_delivery_fee_cents` and 1 500 (the rider's earnings clawback is capped at $15 regardless of the fee) plus an additional 500 cents of customer compensation. This fine creation itself triggers a follow-on debit of the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by `amount_cents` and a recomputation of the rider's `bonus_tier` — the same transitive fan-out chain as the no-show case.\n\nSixth, the owning restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is incremented by `subtotal_cents` minus `final_commission_cents` — the restaurant's slice of the order.\n\nSeventh, the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited with the reconciled `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` (net of any merge discount absorbed by the platform) and the rider's `bonus_tier` is recomputed a final time for the delivery event.\n\nEighth, if the assignment belonged to a `RouteGroup` and every peer assignment in that group has also reached `DELIVERED`, the `RouteGroup` transitions from `ACTIVE` to `COMPLETED`. Otherwise the group stays `ACTIVE` and the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`. A rider only returns to `AVAILABLE` once no active assignments remain for them.\n\nAll of these effects happen as part of the same request. A single rider delivery therefore mutates the assignment, the order, the restaurant, the rider, the fine (when created), and potentially the route group — and each versioned resource in that chain has its `updated_at` refreshed and its `version` incremented exactly once.\n\n### 3.8. Restaurant Settlement\n\nAt each payout cycle, the platform settles with each `ACTIVE` restaurant. A `PlatformAdmin` invokes the restaurant's settle capability; the restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is reset to 0, and the settlement event is treated as the paid-out audit marker. Returns that were approved after a delivery but before the settlement cycle decrement `pending_settlement_cents` at the moment of approval (see §3.9); deliveries increment it. Because both updates are performed atomically as part of the triggering request, the running aggregate is always consistent with the set of `Order` rows in `DELIVERED` that have not been `FULLY_REFUNDED`. The aggregate is never recomputed from scratch; each event applies an incremental delta.\n\n### 3.9. Returns and Refunds\n\nA customer may open a return on a delivered order. The customer-facing payload carries the return's `reason` — one of `QUALITY_ISSUE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `LATE`, or `OTHER` — and a `requested_refund_cents` amount. The request is only eligible when the order is in `DELIVERED` and the current moment is within 24 hours of the order's `actual_delivery_time`; requests outside that window are rejected with `ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED`. The requested refund must be at least 1 and at most the order's `subtotal_cents`; values out of range are rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. A duplicate return attempt — a request made while another `Return` for the same order is already in `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, or `ESCALATED` — is rejected with `ERR_DUPLICATE_RETURN`.\n\nA successful return request creates a `Return` row in `REQUESTED` carrying the `order_id`, the `reason`, the `requested_refund_cents`, and — at decision time — the `reviewer_cs_user_id` that recorded the outcome. The owning `Order` transitions from `DELIVERED` to `REFUND_REQUESTED`. The full set of `Return.status` values is `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, and `ESCALATED`; `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` are terminal.\n\nA `CustomerService` operator then reviews. Approval carries an `approved_refund_cents` amount that must be at least 1, at most the order's `subtotal_cents`, and at most the originally requested refund — any violation is rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. On approval, the `Return` moves to `APPROVED` and the owning order cascades from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `REFUNDED`. The order's `payment_status` becomes `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` if `approved_refund_cents` is strictly less than `subtotal_cents`, or `FULLY_REFUNDED` if the approved amount equals the subtotal. The customer's `credit_balance_cents` is credited by `approved_refund_cents`. The restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is decremented by the same amount. And finally, if the customer's `trust_score` is strictly below 0.5 and the return's `reason` is `QUALITY_ISSUE`, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the customer and whose `reason` is `ABUSIVE_RETURN` with `amount_cents` equal to `approved_refund_cents`. The four possible `Fine.reason` values are `LATE_DELIVERY`, `ABUSIVE_RETURN`, `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT`, and `RIDER_NO_SHOW`; a fine's `subject_type` is one of `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER` and its `subject_id` is the matching entity's `id`. A fine's `settlement_status` begins at `PENDING` and can move to `SETTLED` (when the underlying wallet or settlement event has cleared the balance) or `WAIVED` (when a `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` forgives the debit and reverses any wallet or credit adjustment).\n\nRejection by a `CustomerService` operator moves the `Return` to `REJECTED` and reverts the order from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `DELIVERED` with no monetary change. Escalation moves the `Return` from `REQUESTED` to `ESCALATED` and opens a `WorkOrder` linked via `related_return_id` for supervisor attention. An escalated return can be brought back to `REQUESTED` through a reopen step — this closes the linked `WorkOrder`. The approve / reject transitions accept both `REQUESTED` and `ESCALATED` as legal starting states; the reopen transition is only legal from `ESCALATED`.","numLines":100,"startLine":140,"totalLines":330}}}
